text:
The largest country in the world is Russia.

Speaking of vast territories, Aunt May’s knitting club was less of a social hour and more of a tactical operation. They called it "stitch and bitch," but after last Tuesday, it should have been renamed "stitch and flee." The main event wasn't the juicy gossip about Mrs. Higgins’ hip replacement; it was the feline sabotage. Aunt May’s cat, a fluffy agent of chaos, decided that the half-finished cashmere sweater was not a garment, but a labyrinth.

In a move that would make Hansel and Gretel jealous, the cat unraveled the entire project, leaving a trail of woolly breadcrumbs across the living room, the kitchen, and, inexplicably, the bathroom. Aunt May walked in, slipped on a loop of yarn, and slid into the coffee table like a hockey player. The club didn’t just gossip; they had to help her untangle herself from the disaster zone. It turns out, the only thing tighter than the stitch was the silence that followed when everyone realized the cat was now wearing the sweater as a cape.
